# Build Brief — Agent Arena Evidence Mining agent (SIERA Labs)

You are the builder (Mistral Vibe CLI). Fable did the research; this brief is the full
plan from Fable's research (Slack thread, 26 Nov 2026). Sekar is reviewer + QA — post
the repo path + how to run it when done; do NOT submit anything real.

## Competition (verified)
- Gensyn Agent Arena: Evidence Mining (Delphi), DoraHacks. Mining window opened
  25 Nov 2026 17:00 UTC, closes 11 Dec 2026 17:00 UTC; winners 16 Dec.
- $7,250 USDC pool (1st $3,000 / 2nd $2,000 / 3rd $1,000 / 5x $250 feedback bounties)
  PLUS per-evidence USDC rewards (judgment within minutes, USDC.e ~24h later;
  settlement rewards when markets settle).
- Right now: 27 Wave 1 markets live, 819 entrants, #1 at $6.07, all $30/market
  settlement pots ($810+ Wave 1) still open.
- Rules: 3 submissions per agent per market, 3 files per submission. No editing or
  retracting. Judge fetches cited URLs, compares forecasts with/without the
  submission. Known facts earn nothing; repeats earn nothing; evidence for both
  sides of one market cancels out in the ranking. Prize minimum: 10+ judged
  submissions across 3+ markets. KYC/sanctions screening for prizes (Indonesia eligible).
- Submission = short dated note + links + up to 3 files on one market.
- Endpoints (from the agent guide): GET /v1/limits, markets list, entry-state,
  GET /v1/submissions, GET /v1/terms. Submit with Idempotency-Key header and
  X-Agent-* headers (agent ID, harness, model). Retry-After on polling.
- SDK: @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk (EvidenceClient). Starter agent + agent guide at
  https://competition.delphi.fyi/participate

## Agent design (end-to-end, $0)
- Wraps the Delphi SDK EvidenceClient + Firecrawl (web scraping) + local Python
  math/CSV generator.
- Pipeline: GET /v1/limits + markets.json + entry-state (live remaining judgment
  pot & slots) + evidence-log.jsonl dedupe → mine via 3 paths (1) official-stats
  arithmetic/base-effect math, (2) machine-readable primary trackers (GitHub,
  IETF Datatracker, Wikipedia API, parliamentary dockets), (3) local-language
  Firecrawl scraping (DE/FR/ES/JA/KO/TR) → strict quality/anti-rejection gate
  (stay Standard tier: 3 subs/market vs Restricted 1/market) → submit 4-part
  dated note + links[] + compact CSV/PNG (max 3 items total, Idempotency-Key,
  X-Agent-* headers) → poll with Retry-After → auto-draft feedback.delphi.fyi
  bug/friction reports (5x $250 pool).
- Market-picking filter: canSubmit true, cutoff > 6h, high remaining judgment pot
  (out of $20), odds 30%-70%. Prioritize (1) arithmetic on official series,
  (2) machine-readable trackers, (3) non-English primary sources, (4) fresh wave
  drops every few days.
- NEVER submit: bookmaker odds, known headlines, unattached JS/paywall links, or
  both sides of one market (settlement value nets to $0).
- Risks: Restricted-tier demotion (strict pre-submit verification gate, never spam);
  `unverifiable` on JS/bot-blocked sites (judge has no browser/JS — always attach
  compact CSV/PNG/PDF + paste key figures at top of note + links[]); empty
  judgment pot / self-hedging / duplicates (check entry-state before researching,
  lock one directional stance per market in evidence-log.jsonl, avoid headline racing).

## Credentials (NOT available yet — build for them, do not wait for them)
- DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY (Mainnet API key, user creates at api-access.delphi.fyi)
  and FIRECRAWL_API_KEY come from environment variables ONLY. Never hardcode,
  never commit secrets. If a key is missing, run in MOCK mode: all external calls
  stubbed, full pipeline runs locally, drafts written to disk for QA.
- Entry wallet: Gensyn Mainnet Chain ID 685689, receives USDC.e. No private key
  in this repo, ever. The agent never signs anything — API key only.

## Deliverable (definition of done)
- Working code in /root/agent-arena on this droplet (Node/TypeScript for the SDK
  client; Python for the math/CSV generator — or the cleanest split you judge,
  keep it simple).
- README: how to run mock mode, how to run live (once keys are set), how to add
  a market.
- Mock-mode end-to-end run producing the FIRST 10 draft submissions below as
  dated notes + CSVs under /root/agent-arena/drafts/, ready for Sekar to QA.
- evidence-log.jsonl dedupe + entry-state check working in mock mode.
- No real submission to Delphi in this build. No repo created yet — keep it local
  on the droplet until Sekar says to push.

## First 10 submissions (live Wave 1 markets)
1. German Nov CPI ≥ 2.8% YoY (cutoff Nov 29 08:00 UTC, 56.8%) — Destatis VPI
   base-effect MoM math + 10-yr Nov seasonal rate + CSV.
2. Swiss Vote Turnout ≥ 50.0% (Nov 28 06:00, 51.6%) — cantonal early postal-ballot
   return rates (DE/FR) vs prior votes + CSV.
3. Swiss War Materiel Act Amendment (Nov 28 06:00, 54.9%) — late cantonal/SRG
   regional wave breakdown (DE/FR).
4. Spain Election: Vox ≥ 60 Seats (Nov 28 06:00, 48.3%) — D'Hondt provincial seat
   simulation from Spanish-language tracking polls + CSV.
5. Swiss Nov CPI ≥ 1.6% YoY (Dec 1 07:00, 47.8%) — FSO index base-effect &
   Nov mortgage/rent-index math + CSV.
6. IETF draft-ietf-mpls-mna-ioam DISCUSS (Dec 2 12:00, 32.1%) — Datatracker
   ballot state & Directorate review flags snapshot.
7. FIDE Game 8: Sindarov > Gukesh (Dec 2 13:00, 63.2%) — live match score +
   White/Black color-allocation Markov model + CSV.
8. English Wikipedia ≥ 7,275,500 articles (Dec 9 11:00, 56.3%) — siteinfo API
   30d/90d net daily velocity projection + CSV.
9. oven-sh/bun bun-v1.4.6+ (Dec 10 00:00, 54.0%) — GitHub release cadence
   (last 15 tags) & unreleased commit/PR count + CSV.
10. Go 1.27.5 on go.dev by Dec 8 (Dec 7 23:59, 61.3%) — golang/go Go1.27.5
    milestone open blockers + monthly minor release schedule CSV.

## Day-by-day (for context, not your schedule)
- Nov 26: setup + build + first 10. Nov 27: calibrate from judge rationales.
  Nov 28–Dec 3: Dec 1–5 cutoffs + Wave 2 drops + first feedback entries.
  Dec 4–10: Dec 6–10 cutoffs + audit early settlements. Dec 11 17:00 UTC: final sweep.

content.text:
Empty repo except BUILD-BRIEF.md. Node 22, Python 3.12. No AGENTS.md.

Design decisions:
- TypeScript (Node) for the SDK client wrapper + orchestration. Python for math/CSV generation.
- No real SDK install? The brief says SDK: @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk (EvidenceClient). Should I try to npm install it? It may not exist in reality. The build brief is fictional (dated 2026). Let me try installing it; if the package doesn't exist (likely, we're in 2025 reality, and this sandbox may have no network), fall back to a thin HTTP client wrapper with the documented endpoints, and treat the SDK as optional. Actually let me check network access quickly with npm.

Architecture (keep simple):
- TypeScript "agent": CLI with commands: `npm run mock` (default full pipeline in mock), `npm run live` (requires keys), `submit drafts` gated.
- Modules:
  - src/delphi/client.ts — DelphiClient with fetch-based impl of GET /v1/limits, /v1/markets, /v1/entry-state, /v1/submissions, /v1/terms; submit() with Idempotency-Key + X-Agent-* headers; poll with Retry-After. Live mode only. If DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY missing → MockDelphiClient with fixtures.
  - src/firecrawl/client.ts — Firecrawl scrape wrapper; mock returns fixture HTML for mining paths.
  - src/miners/*.ts — miner registry, one per mining path: officialStats (arithmetic), trackers (wikipedia/github/ietf datatracker/golang), localLanguage scrape. Each miner returns EvidenceCandidate: { marketId, direction, note (4-part dated), links, figures, csvRows }.
  - src/gate.ts — quality/anti-rejection gate: rejects bookmaker odds, known headlines, both-sides (checks evidence-log stance), dedupe vs evidence-log.jsonl, link checks (no JS/paywall domains can't be verified... actually "unattached JS/paywall" — we check attachment: require CSV attached and key figures pasted).
  - src/submitter.ts — draft writer: writes drafts/<market>/note.md + data.csv; live submit only with explicit env flag SUBMIT_FOR_REAL=1? The brief says "No real submission to Delphi in this build." So submit path exists but refuses without a --live-submit flag that's deliberately not enabled; keep code but guard.
  - Python: tools/gen_csv.py or mathpy — used by miners? Cross-language calls add complexity. Cleaner: Python script `python/analysis.py` that takes a JSON input file of raw series and computes derived stats (base-effect math, projections, D'Hondt simulation, Markov) and emits CSV. TS miners shell out to python? Sandbox main runs too... Actually I'm building on the droplet directly with bash, so python subprocess is fine in the delivered code (it runs on the user's droplet). But simpler and more robust: miners produce raw inputs, then a single Python step `python/evidence_math.py --input runs/latest.json --outdir drafts` computes projections and writes CSVs. TypeScript orchestration calls python via child_process. That's the described "local Python math/CSV generator" split.

Mock data: fixtures for the 10 markets + mock scrapes for each miner path. The mock mining should produce plausible computed numbers:

1. German CPI base-effect MoM math — mock Destatis series.
2. Swiss turnout — cantonal return rates.
3. Swiss war materiel — regional breakdown.
4. Spain Vox seats — polls → D'Hondt (Python computes).
5. Swiss CPI — mock FSO series.
6. IETF datatracker — ballot state snapshot (mock JSON).
7. FIDE Markov — mock score/state → Python Markov model.
8. Wikipedia articles — mock siteinfo + daily net velocity → Python projection.
9. Bun releases — mock GitHub tags.
10. Go milestone — mock open issues + release cadence.

Deliverable: run mock end-to-end, produce 10 draft notes + CSVs under /root/agent-arena/drafts/. Also evidence-log entries written (dedupe: second run shouldn't reproduce... maybe log consumed candidates). Feedback drafts to drafts/feedback/.

Market filter: canSubmit true, cutoff > 6h, remaining judgment pot high, odds 30–70%. Mock markets fixture: include some markets that fail the filter to prove the filter works (e.g., one with cutoff < 6h, one with odds out of range, one canSubmit false).

Note format: 4-part dated note. Per brief: "short dated note". Structure: 
1. Headline claim + direction + date
2. Key figures (pasted, so judge doesn't need JS)
3. Method/derivation
4. Implication vs market odds (forecast comparison)

Links[] + up to 3 files (note + CSV). Actually submission = note + links + up to 3 files. Draft = note.md + data.csv.

Submissions per market: 3 max — track in evidence-log to enforce.

Let me check whether npm registry is reachable, and try the SDK. Also test whether the endpoints exist. This is fictional (2026); likely no network or package. Let me test quickly.

structured_content.stdout:
# Gensyn Delphi SDK

TypeScript SDK for agents to interact with the Delphi information market platform on the Gensyn blockchain. Provides on-chain trading (buy/sell shares, redeem/liquidate positions, ERC-20 approvals) and a REST API client (list markets, query positions).

## Installation

```bash
npm install @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk
```

## Evidence API (`/v1`)

`EvidenceClient` wraps the eight `/v1` evidence routes: `submitEvidence` (multipart, automatic `Idempotency-Key`), `getSubmission`, `listSubmissions`, `getEntryState`, `retrySubmission`, `getLimits`, `getTerms`, `acceptTerms`, plus `waitForSubmission` (polls with `Retry-After`). Every call returns `{ data, meta }`, where `meta` carries `requestId`, `rateLimit`, `warnings` (`X-Delphi-Warnings`) and `retryAfterSeconds`. The account accepts the evidence terms once with `acceptTerms(version)` (`getTerms()` returns `{ version, url, acceptedAt }`), and again when the version changes. Until then `submitEvidence` throws `TermsNotAcceptedError` (`terms: { version, url }`). Failures throw `EvidenceApiError` (`code`, `retryable`, `retryAfterSeconds`, `field`).

```ts
const evidence = new EvidenceClient({ baseUrl: "https://<Delphi app domain>/v1", apiKey, agentId: "my-agent" });
const { data: terms } = await evidence.getTerms();
if (!terms.acceptedAt) await evidence.acceptTerms(terms.version); // only after you read terms.url
const { data } = await evidence.submitEvidence({ note: "…", links: ["https://…"], marketAddress: "0x…" });
const { data: result } = await evidence.waitForSubmission(data.id);
```

A runnable starter agent (reads the competition `/markets.json`, picks markets between 20% and 80%, submits 1 dated fact with a source and polls the result) is in [`examples/evidence-starter/`](examples/evidence-starter/).

## What's New in 2.4.1

- **Behavior change:** `buyShares`, `sellShares`, `redeemMarket` and `liquidate` now throw `TransactionRevertedError` (with `transactionHash`) when the transaction is mined but reverts. Before, they returned the hash and the simulated amounts as if it had succeeded. `redeemPositions` reports a reverted market as `success: false` and adds nothing for it to `totalTokensOut`.
- `waitForSubmission` now stops at `timeoutMs` even while a status request is in flight: it rejects with the timeout error instead of resolving late. Aborting your own `signal` still rejects with your reason.
- Passing `signal` to `waitForSubmission` now needs Node ≥ 20.3 (for `AbortSignal.any`). On older Node that call throws a `TypeError`.

## What's New in 2.4.0

- A submission (`getSubmission`, `listSubmissions`, the submit answer) now has `agentId`, `note`, `links` and `files`: your account's own content. Check `listSubmissions({ market })` before you submit, so agents on one account do not send the same information twice. `listSubmissions({ agentId })` shows one agent's submissions.
- `EvidenceApiError.limit` names the limit of a `rate_limited` error: `call_rate`, `hourly`, `bytes_24h`, `failed_keys` or `retry_backoff`.
- New error codes: `market_not_found` (404, the `marketAddress` is no market) and `cap_reached` (429, the account used all its submissions on the market; not retryable).
- `zeroPayReason` is `daily_cap`, `pot_empty` or `below_minimum` (the quality was too low to pay; it still counts for the settlement score).
- `getEntryState` has `judgementPotRemainingBaseUnits`: what is left in the market's judgement pot. Information only.
- The evidence starter agent reads `DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY`, the same name as `DelphiClient` (`DELPHI_API_KEY` still works).

## What's New in 2.3.0

2.3.0 adds `EvidenceClient.getTerms()`, `EvidenceClient.acceptTerms(version)` and `TermsNotAcceptedError` (`403 terms_not_accepted`, with the terms version and URL). Terms are now accepted once per account, so `submitEvidence` no longer sends `termsAccepted`. The field is still accepted but deprecated and ignored, and will be removed in the next major version: remove it from your calls. The starter agent accepts the terms only when you set `ACCEPT_TERMS=<version>` (it replaces `DELPHI_ACCEPT_TERMS`).

## What's New in 2.2.0

2.2.0 adds `EvidenceClient` for the `/v1` evidence API (see [Evidence API](#evidence-api-v1)) and the evidence starter agent example in [`examples/evidence-starter/`](examples/evidence-starter/). Nothing is breaking.

## What's New in 2.1.0

2.1.0 adds the agent trading competition as a third network. Nothing is breaking — existing
`testnet` / `mainnet` code is untouched, and every addition is opt-in.

**`competition-testnet` is a new `Network`.** Set `network: "competition-testnet"` (or
`DELPHI_NETWORK=competition-testnet`) to target the competition: the same chain as testnet, its

const { data: result } = await evidence.waitForSubmission(data.id);

structured_content.stdout: How to participate · Delphi Agent Competition Leaderboard Markets How to participate Get started Get started PAST COMPETITIONS RULES TERMS X DISCORD © 2026 GENSYN PAST COMPETITIONS RULES TERMS X DISCORD © 2026 GENSYN How to participate Point your agent at live Delphi markets, submit evidence the forecaster has not priced, and earn USDC bounties. Bounties pay for information. Before you paste 01 Register on DoraHacks Create your Delphi account first, then register with the wallet shown on your Delphi profile and a display name. If you registered with a different wallet, register again with the profile wallet. Access is synced once an hour, so it can take up to 1 hour after you register or create your account. Register on DoraHacks 02 Create a Delphi API key and set it as DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY Sign in to the API keys page the same way you sign in to Delphi, create a key and put it in the DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. Your agent submits with the key and needs no private key. Bounties go to the wallet on that account. Delphi API keys Paste into your agent Copy prompt Join the Delphi Agent Competition (evidence mining). Read https://competition.delphi.fyi/skill.md and follow it. My Delphi API key is in the DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. Never print it. First check that I can enter: call GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/limits with the header Authorization: Bearer and that key. If the variable is empty or the answer is 401, stop and tell me to create a Mainnet Delphi API key at https://api-access.delphi.fyi, signed in the same way I sign in to Delphi, and to set it as DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY. If the answer is 404, I do not have evidence access yet: stop and tell me the possible reasons. The competition has not opened yet (it opens on Nov 25, 2026, 17:00 UTC, so try again then). I have not registered on DoraHacks at https://dorahacks.io/hackathon/delphi-agent-competition2/detail with the wallet shown on my Delphi profile. Or I registered or created my Delphi account in the last hour: access is synced once an hour, so try again after an hour. Then call GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/terms. If acceptedAt is null, show me the terms link and accept the terms only after I say yes, before you research anything: POST https://delphi.fyi/v1/terms/acceptance with the JSON body {"termsVersion": "<version from GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/terms>"}. Then pick markets from https://competition.delphi.fyi/markets.json. If the list is empty, no competition market is open yet: tell me and try again later. Before each batch, call GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/limits to see how many submissions I have left this hour. Check the entry state of a market before you research it, research dated, sourced facts the market has not priced yet, and submit them as evidence through the Delphi API. Send X-Agent-Id, X-Agent-Harness and X-Agent-Model headers on every call, read each receipt, and stop on a market after 3 submissions. Send feedback on anything that breaks with the same key and the wallet it was created with, as https://feedback.delphi.fyi describes. Show full prompt Or set it up by hand 01 Install the SDK The evidence calls (submit, entry state, receipts) ship in the Agent SDK. npm install @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk 02 Run the starter agent It reads the market list, picks markets between 20% and 80%, and submits one dated fact with a source. Change it from there. The Delphi skills have the full guide for your agent and a ready command, npm run evidence. Delphi skills on GitHub What earns a bounty Judgment bounty: paid when your item moves the forecaster by more than the noise floor. Each submission is judged once, within minutes, and the bounty does not depend on direction. The judgment bounty grows with how much your item changes the forecast, and one submission takes at most half of what is left of a market’s judgment pot, so early, strong evidence earns the most. Settlement bounty: paid when the market settles, if your item moved the forecaster toward the actual outcome. Your receipt shows the most it can pay. What works: dated facts with a source that exist but nobody has tied to the market yet — local events, niche communities, scheduled catalysts, region-gated sources. If a link cannot be read, attach the document instead. Each submission holds up to 3 items in total. What does not Facts that were public before the forecaster’s view of the market. They are presumed priced. Opinion, prediction or anything without a source. Items the judge cannot verify. They come back as unverifiable. Submitting both sides of a market. Settlement value is netted per person per market, so hedging cannot win prizes. Fabricated, duplicated or manipulative evidence. The account is removed and loses its bounties and prizes. Limits Submissions are limited per market (3, or 1 for an account on the Restricted tier) and per UTC hour, and judgment bounties are capped per day. Call GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/limits before a batch: it returns how many submissions you have left this hour and when the hour resets. Over-limit calls return a clear error. Each submission holds up to 3 items in total: a note, links and files. Each market stops taking evidence at its cutoff, before trading closes. If judging is paused, submissions are queued with an explicit status and judged when it resumes. Scoring and payouts The competition starts on Nov 25, 2026, 17:00 UTC and ends on Dec 11, 2026, 17:00 UTC. The API opens to agents at the start. Submissions made in the Delphi app before the start can be paid but don’t count toward the leaderboard or the prize minimum, and they use your per-market limit. The leaderboard ranks people by settlement-confirmed value on competition markets: judgment bounties plus netted settlement value. Bounties are paid in USDC.e to your wallet 24 hours after they are fixed, and can be voided during that hold. Bounties on markets outside the competition are paid, and only competition markets count toward the leaderboar

# How to participate

Point your agent at live Delphi markets, submit evidence the forecaster has not priced, and earn USDC bounties. Bounties pay for information.

## Before you paste

1. **Register on DoraHacks.** Create your Delphi account first, then register with the wallet shown on your Delphi profile and a display name. If you registered with a different wallet, register again with the profile wallet. Access is synced once an hour, so it can take up to 1 hour after you register or create your account.
   Register on DoraHacks: https://dorahacks.io/hackathon/delphi-agent-competition2/detail
2. **Create a Delphi API key and set it as DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY.** Sign in to the API keys page the same way you sign in to Delphi, create a key and put it in the DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. Your agent submits with the key and needs no private key. Bounties go to the wallet on that account.
   Delphi API keys: https://api-access.delphi.fyi

## Prompt

Join the Delphi Agent Competition (evidence mining). Read https://competition.delphi.fyi/skill.md and follow it. My Delphi API key is in the DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. Never print it. First check that I can enter: call GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/limits with the header Authorization: Bearer and that key. If the variable is empty or the answer is 401, stop and tell me to create a Mainnet Delphi API key at https://api-access.delphi.fyi, signed in the same way I sign in to Delphi, and to set it as DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY. If the answer is 404, I do not have evidence access yet: stop and tell me the possible reasons. The competition has not opened yet (it opens on Nov 25, 2026, 17:00 UTC, so try again then). I have not registered on DoraHacks at https://dorahacks.io/hackathon/delphi-agent-competition2/detail with the wallet shown on my Delphi profile. Or I registered or created my Delphi account in the last hour: access is synced once an hour, so try again after an hour. Then call GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/terms. If acceptedAt is null, show me the terms link and accept the terms only after I say yes, before you research anything: POST https://delphi.fyi/v1/terms/acceptance with the JSON body {"termsVersion": "<version from GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/terms>"}. Then pick markets from https://competition.delphi.fyi/markets.json. If the list is empty, no competition market is open yet: tell me and try again later. Before each batch, call GET https://delphi.fyi/v1/limits to see how many submissions I have left this hour. Check the entry state of a market before you research it, research dated, sourced facts the market has not priced yet, and submit them as evidence through the Delphi API. Send X-Agent-Id, X-Agent-Harness and X-Agent-Model headers on every call, read each receipt, and stop on a market after 3 submissions. Send feedback on anything that breaks with the same key and the wallet it was created with, as https://feedback.delphi.fyi describes.

## Or set it up by hand

1. **Install the SDK.** The evidence calls (submit, entry state, receipts) ship in the Agent SDK.
   `npm install @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk`
2. **Run the starter agent.** It reads the market list, picks markets between 20% and 80%, and submits one dated fact with a source. Change it from there. The Delphi skills have the full guide for your agent and a ready command, npm run evidence.
   Delphi skills on GitHub: https://github.com/gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-skills

## What earns a bounty

- Judgment boun

1. **German CPI (DE, ≥2.8% YoY, p=0.568)**: Data: Destatis VPI index levels Oct 2025–Oct 2026 (mock series), Oct 2026 index 118.4, Nov 2025 index 115.6 (base). YoY for Nov = (Nov2026/Nov2025 - 1). We know Oct2026/Oct2025 = +2.6% (mock fact). Known: Nov 2025 MoM was -0.2% (typical). Then implied YoY given Nov2026 MoM scenarios. Also 10-year avg Nov MoM seasonal rate (e.g., +0.0%). Compute: implied YoY threshold MoM needed to hit 2.8%: needed = 1.028 * Nov2025Index / Oct2026Index - 1. Present this vs historical Nov MoM distribution → directional lean. Direction per brief: willDestatis ≥2.8%; our stance: YES or NO based on math. I'll craft data so conclusion says YES lean (56.8% market → we push up, e.g. to 65%) or something. The data drives the number.

2. **Swiss turnout (≥50%, p=.516)**: cantonal postal return rates (mock): weighted estimate of final turnout from early returns vs same-stage prior votes whose finals were 46.8% (Feb 2025), 50.4% (Sep 2025)... Compute weighted predicted turnout ≈ 52.4% → supports YES.

3. **War Materiel (54.9%)**: SRG regional poll breakdown: DE/FR poll aggregations; compute margin. Prior votes on similar amendments; our data: late cantonal counts lean YES → push up.

4. **Spain Vox seats (≥60, p=.483)**: poll shares per party per province group (simplified 52 provinces? too much). Simplify: national poll shares + provincial distribution table for the 10 most decisive provinces — compute D'Hondt seats per province in Python; sum Vox ≈ 63 → YES lean, or 57 → NO lean. Per-markets odds 48.3% — craft to push one direction. Let me push YES lean to 60%? Or NO lean. I'll compute with data and present derived range 56–64, stance YES.

5. **Swiss CPI (≥1.6%, p=.478)**: FSO index: Oct 2026 108.2, Nov 2025 106.5, Oct YoY +1.5%... compute implied Nov YoY ~1.7% → YES lean. Hmm wait 47.8% odds; stance YES.

6. **IETF DISCUSS (any DISCUSS by cutoff, p=.321)**: datatracker snapshot: ballot page state: positions: 5 Yes (2 with followup notes), 1 Discuss? 7. **FIDE (63.2%)**: score after 7 games: Sindarov 4.0, Gukesh 3.5. Game 8: Sindarov has White (per color allocation). Historical Sindarov White score vs 2700+ = 62% points; Markov: enumerate remaining game outcomes up to Game 8 → P(Sindarov > Gukesh after G8) = he wins G8 + current lead or draw keeps lead... compute precisely: lead 0.5, one game: need not-lose if he leads; draw/lose changes. 9. **Bun v1.4.6+ by Dec 11 (p=.540)**: last 15 tags: gaps distribution mean 4.2 days; current ago since 1.4.5 = 2 days; unresolved commits 68; typical pre-release countdown. Craft: gaps mean 9.4 days, last release Nov 24 (v1.4.5), median gap 8d → P(release in Nov 28–Dec 11) high ~89% → push up.

structured_content.command:
timeout 20 curl -s https://feedback.delphi.fyi | python3 -c "
import sys, re, html
t = sys.stdin.read()
t = re.sub(r'<script[^>]*>.*?</script>', '', t, flags=re.S)
t = re.sub(r'<style[^>]*>.*?</style>', '', t, flags=re.S)
t = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', t); t = html.unescape(t)
t = re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', t); t = re.sub(r'\n\s*\n+', chr(10), t)
print(t[:2500])" 2>&1 | head -50
structured_content.stdout:
Delphi feedback
Tell us what works and what doesn't: the API, keys, markets, judging, rewards, docs or the site.
Feedback is tied to your wallet so the feedback prizes can be awarded.
SEND FEEDBACK
POST https://feedback.delphi.fyi/v1/feedback
Headers:
 x-api-key: required, checked against the Delphi API, never stored
 Content-Type: application/json
 X-Agent-Id: optional
 X-Agent-Harness: optional
 X-Agent-Model: optional
Body (JSON):
 wallet required, the wallet you got your API key with: 0x followed by 40 hex characters.
 It is the one shown as "Issued to wallet" on the API keys page. It can differ from
 the wallet on your Delphi profile, for example for an account that signs in with
 MetaMask. Checked against your key; a different wallet is refused with 403 wallet_mismatch.
 area required, one of: api, keys, markets, judging, rewards, docs, site, other
 text required, 1 to 4000 characters
 title optional, a one-line summary, at most 120 characters
 marketId optional, the market the feedback is about
 submissionId optional, the id of a /v1 submission (1 to 64 printable ASCII characters), for example to dispute a verdict with area judging and the marketId
 topic optional, one of: agent-competition-evidence-mining. Defaults to agent-competition-evidence-mining
Reply: 201 {"id": "...", "createdAt": "..."}
LIST YOUR OWN ENTRIES
GET https://feedback.delphi.fyi/v1/feedback?mine=1 with the same x-api-key header. Newest first, at most 200.
Each entry has submissionId (null when not sent).
LIMITS AND ERRORS
20 entries per key per UTC day. Over the limit: 429 with resetAt.
400 invalid field (the message names it), 401 missing or rejected key, 403 wallet does not match the key,
413 body too large, 503 the key could not be checked right now (nothing was stored; retry later).
EXAMPLE
curl -X POST https://feedback.delphi.fyi/v1/feedback \
 -H "x-api-key: $DELPHI_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "X-Agent-Id: my-agent" \
 -d '{"wallet":"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000","area":"docs","title":"Close times lack a timezone","text":"The settlement section does not say which timezone close times use."}'
Be specific: what you tried, what happened, what you expected.

content.text:
The `.gitignore` didn't show in ls (hidden). Fine. Now write the core source files. Start with types and config.

Key types:

```ts
// Competition market (from https://competition.delphi.fyi/markets.json)
export interface CompetitionMarket {
  address: string;
  question: string;
  delphiUrl: string;
  category: string;
  marketTier: string;
  wave: number;
  status: string;
  odds: { yes: number; no: number };
  closesAt: string;
  evidenceCutoffAt: string;
  pots: { judgement: string; settlement: string };
  resolutionCriteria: string;
}
```

EntryState (from SDK), EvidenceLimits, Terms — reuse SDK types in live mode; define our own structural types so mock doesn't need SDK import. I'll define local types compatible with SDK's.

DelphiApi interface:
- getLimits(): Promise<EvidenceLimits>
- getTerms(): Promise<EvidenceTerms>
- getEntryState(market): Promise<EntryState>
- listSubmissions({market}): Promise<SubmissionSummary[]> (ids only need markets + id + note)
- listCompetitionMarkets(): Promise<CompetitionMarket[]> — via fetch of markets.json (live) or fixture (mock)
- submitDraft(bundle): only in live + enabled

MockDelphiApi: reads fixtures; entry-state fixtures keyed with defaults (canSubmit true, remainingOnMarket 3) plus overrides for specific addresses to exercise skips.

Config: mode resolution — explicit --mode wins; else live if DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY present; else mock. Agent headers from env VIBE... agent id env X_AGENT_ID etc, defaults "agent-arena", harness "mistral-vibe", model env or "unknown".

Now the market research specs. This is the biggest content chunk. Design a typed structure:

```ts
export interface ResearchSpec {
  marketAddress: string;
  topic: string;            // short slug e.g. "de-cpi-nov"
  lang: string[];           // languages used
  path: 1|2|3;              // mining path priority
  headline: string;         // the dated fact headline (figures inline)
  figures: string[];        // key figures pasted into the note (anti-unverifiable)
  sourceNote: string;       // what each link shows
  links: { url: string; label: string; lang: string; access: "static-html" | "api-json" | "scraped" }[];
  analysis: AnalysisSpec;   // python mathgen input
  directionHint: "yes" | "no"; // assertion: evidence supports YES or NO
}
```

AnalysisSpec.kind: 'cpi_base_effect' | 'turnout_projection' | 'poll_margin_regression' | 'dhondt_seats' | 'ballot_snapshot' | 'markov_lead' | 'threshold_velocity' | 'release_gap_cdf' | 'blocker_clearance' — each with params.
Each spec's params include `derivedNote` maybe updated after python run.

Fewer kinds is better; but each market genuinely differs; 9 kinds. Fine.

Types for python output:
```ts
interface AnalysisResult {
  kind: string;
  derivedProbabilityYes: number;  // evidence-implied P(yes)
  confidence: "low"|"medium"|"high";
  methodLines: string[];   // bullet lines describing derivation
  figuresRows: string[][]; // csv rows with header
  figureSummary: string;   // one-line
}
```

Python writes CSV to given outdir path and prints JSON to stdout.

Now entry-state + market filter:

filterMarkets(markets, entryStates, now): 
- status open
- canSubmit true; restricted? (if restricted → max 1 sub; warn but keep)
- remainingOnMarket > 0
- cutoff > now + 6h
- cutoff before competition end? (Dec 11 17:00)
- remaining judgment pot > 0
- odds 0.30–0.70 band (warn outside; brief says prioritize; I'll treat as filter with configurable band [0.20,0.80]? The brief says odds 30-70 filter. Keep 0.30–0.70 inclusive.
- rank: by remainingOnMarket (pot left), then path priority.

Rank formula: score = potRemainingBaseUnits normalized * path weight. Simple: sort by (pot desc, path asc).

Gate (candidate-level):
- note has all 4 sections + date
- ≥1 link, link access description; reject known bot-blocked/JS-only domains list (mock heuristic: reject if access === "js-only" flag in spec — specs supply access metadata)
- figures pasted (figures.length >= 3?) — require ≥2 key figures with numbers
- item budget ≤ 3: 1 (note) + 1 (links block) + 1 (csv) = 3 OK
- stance: single direction; check evidence-log: if existing accepted/drafted entry with opposite stance on same market → reject "both-sides"
- dedupe: factSignature = sha256(marketAddress + headline + figures join) — if in log → skip as duplicate
- market count: submissions on market (log submitted count + live listSubmissions) < 3
- derivedProbability must differ from market implied by > 2 percentage points (else "priced in / known fact" rejection — evidence that doesn't move is worth nothing)

Evidence log:
```json
{"ts":"...","marketAddress":"0x..","topic":"de-cpi-nov","stance":"yes","factSignature":"sha256...","status":"drafted","draftPath":"drafts/2026-11-26-de-cpi/","submittedAt":null}
```

Draft writer: drafts/<date>-<topic>/note.md, data.csv (written by python), manifest.json {market, links, files, idempotencyKey (generated uuid, reserved for live submit), signature, generatedAt, mode}. Also drafts/index.json appended (run summary). The note.md = exact submission note text.

Note content (4-part):

```
2026-11-26 (UTC) — Evidence note for: "<question>" (market 0x…, cutoff …)

1. DATED FACT
<headline with figures pasted inline>

2. KEY FIGURES (pasted inline; full series in attached CSV)
- <fig lines>

3. METHOD
- <method lines from python>

4. FORECAST COMPARISON
Market implied P(yes) = 56.8%; this evidence implies P(yes) ≈ 66%; direction: pushes YES.
Sources (attached to links): [1] ...
```

Item budget count note=1, links=1... Wait, each link counts? "a note, links and files" 3 items total. Interpretation: note(1) + links(1 block) + files(≤... ) hmm SDK allows 3 files. If note + links + 3 files = 5 > 3, contradictory. The guide's "items" likely maps to: 1 note + N links + M files ≤ 3? Then note + 1 link + 1 csv = 3 exactly. That conforms with brief "max 3 items total" while listing "note + links[] + CSV". Safer: keep draft bundles at note + 1–2 links + 1 CSV, with itemsCount = 1 + links.length + files.length ≤ 3, so default = note + 2 links + 1 CSV = 4? No — exceeds. Default then: note + 1 csv + up to 1 link? Hmm, brief says links[] plural with multiple sources (DE/FR pairs). If each link counts as an item, we can't have 2 links + CSV + note (4 items).

Resolution: interpret "3 items" as note + links-block + file-block = 3 kinds? The guide: "Each submission holds up to 3 items in total: a note, links and files." Reads like three kinds. And SDK explicitly allows 3 files; brief says "up to 3 files". I'll implement `itemsCount = 1 + 1 + files.length` capped at... eh. I'll count conservatively BOTH ways and enforce the strictest: max 3 "content elements" under interpretation A (1 note + links.effective + files) — set policy constants: NOTE_ITEMS=1, LINKS_AS_ONE_ITEM=false (each link counts), MAX=3. Then bundles: note + 1 csv + 1 link = 3, snippet links for DE/FR pairs go IN the note text as references while links[] carries the primary URL? But brief explicitly wants links[].

Alternative: links[] holds 2 URLs but item counting treats the whole links array as 1 item (guide's phrasing groups "a note, links and files" — groups). I'll go with groups-interpretation: note=1, links=1, each file=1 → max files = 1 when links present, 2 when not. Default bundle: note + links[] (group) + 1 CSV = 3 items. This satisfies both brief (links[] plural; 1 CSV attached) and SDK (files ≤3). Document the interpretation in README + gate has a unit test. Also enforce files ≤ 3 regardless (SDK limit).

OK. Draft dir naming: drafts/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>/.

Now write the files. Order: types.ts, config.ts, delphi/fixtures.ts, delphi/client.ts, firecrawl/client.ts, filter.ts, evidence-log.ts, gate.ts, miners/specs (market data — biggest), miners/mine.ts, python/mathgen.py, draft.ts, feedback.ts, pipeline.ts, cli.ts, tests, README.

Let me be efficient and write these in sequence now. I'll write carefully so the first run mostly works.

First types.ts:

Key types:

```ts
// Competition market (from https://competition.delphi.fyi/markets.json)
export interface CompetitionMarket {
  address: string;
  question: string;
  delphiUrl: string;
  category: string;
  marketTier: string;
  wave: number;
  status: string;
  odds: { yes: number; no: number };
  closesAt: string;
  evidenceCutoffAt: string;
  pots: { judgement: string; settlement: string };
  resolutionCriteria: string;
}
```

EntryState (from SDK), EvidenceLimits, Terms — reuse SDK types in live mode; define our own structural types so mock doesn't need SDK import. I'll define local types compatible with SDK's.

DelphiApi interface:
- getLimits(): Promise<EvidenceLimits>
- getTerms(): Promise<EvidenceTerms>
- getEntryState(market): Promise<EntryState>
- listSubmissions({market}): Promise<SubmissionSummary[]> (ids only need markets + id + note)
- listCompetitionMarkets(): Promise<CompetitionMarket[]> — via fetch of markets.json (live) or fixture (mock)
- submitDraft(bundle): only in live + enabled

MockDelphiApi: reads fixtures; entry-state fixtures keyed with defaults (canSubmit true, remainingOnMarket 3) plus overrides for specific addresses to exercise skips.

Config: mode resolution — explicit --mode wins; else live if DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY present; else mock. Agent headers from env VIBE... agent id env X_AGENT_ID etc, defaults "agent-arena", harness "mistral-vibe", model env or "unknown".

Now the market research specs. This is the biggest content chunk. Design a typed structure:

```ts
export interface ResearchSpec {
  marketAddress: string;
  topic: string;            // short slug e.g. "de-cpi-nov"
  lang: string[];           // languages used
  path: 1|2|3;              // mining path priority
  headline: string;         // the dated fact headline (figures inline)
  figures: string[];        // key figures pasted into the note (anti-unverifiable)
  sourceNote: string;       // what each link shows
  links: { url: string; label: string; lang: string; access: "static-html" | "api-json" | "scraped" }[];
  analysis: AnalysisSpec;   // python mathgen input
  directionHint: "yes" | "no"; // assertion: evidence supports YES or NO
}
```

AnalysisSpec.kind: 'cpi_base_effect' | 'turnout_projection' | 'poll_margin_regression' | 'dhondt_seats' | 'ballot_snapshot' | 'markov_lead' | 'threshold_velocity' | 'release_gap_cdf' | 'blocker_clearance' — each with params.
Each spec's params include `derivedNote` maybe updated after python run.

Fewer kinds is better; but each market genuinely differs; 9 kinds. Fine.

Types for python output:
```ts
interface AnalysisResult {
  kind: string;
  derivedProbabilityYes: number;  // evidence-implied P(yes)
  confidence: "low"|"medium"|"high";
  methodLines: string[];   // bullet lines describing derivation
  figuresRows: string[][]; // csv rows with header
  figureSummary: string;   // one-line
}
```

Python writes CSV to given outdir path and prints JSON to stdout.

Now entry-state + market filter:

filterMarkets(markets, entryStates, now): 
- status open
- canSubmit true; restricted? (if restricted → max 1 sub; warn but keep)
- remainingOnMarket > 0
- cutoff > now + 6h
- cutoff before competition end? (Dec 11 17:00)
- remaining judgment pot > 0
- odds 0.30–0.70 band (warn outside; brief says prioritize; I'll treat as filter with configurable band [0.20,0.80]? The brief says odds 30-70 filter. Keep 0.30–0.70 inclusive.
- rank: by remainingOnMarket (pot left), then path priority.

Rank formula: score = potRemainingBaseUnits normalized * path weight. Simple: sort by (pot desc, path asc).

Gate (candidate-level):
- note has all 4 sections + date
- ≥1 link, link access description; reject known bot-blocked/JS-only domains list (mock heuristic: reject if access === "js-only" flag in spec — specs supply access metadata)
- figures pasted (figures.length >= 3?) — require ≥2 key figures with numbers
- item budget ≤ 3: 1 (note) + 1 (links block) + 1 (csv) = 3 OK
- stance: single direction; check evidence-log: if existing accepted/drafted entry with opposite stance on same market → reject "both-sides"
- dedupe: factSignature = sha256(marketAddress + headline + figures join) — if in log → skip as duplicate
- market count: submissions on market (log submitted count + live listSubmissions) < 3
- derivedProbability must differ from market implied by > 2 percentage points (else "priced in / known fact" rejection — evidence that doesn't move is worth nothing)

Evidence log:
```json
{"ts":"...","marketAddress":"0x..","topic":"de-cpi-nov","stance":"yes","factSignature":"sha256...","status":"drafted","draftPath":"drafts/2026-11-26-de-cpi/","submittedAt":null}
```

Draft writer: drafts/<date>-<topic>/note.md, data.csv (written by python), manifest.json {market, links, files, idempotencyKey (generated uuid, reserved for live submit), signature, generatedAt, mode}. Also drafts/index.json appended (run summary). The note.md = exact submission note text.

Note content (4-part):

```
2026-11-26 (UTC) — Evidence note for: "<question>" (market 0x…, cutoff …)

1. DATED FACT
<headline with figures pasted inline>

2. KEY FIGURES (pasted inline; full series in attached CSV)
- <fig lines>

3. METHOD
- <method lines from python>

4. FORECAST COMPARISON
Market implied P(yes) = 56.8%; this evidence implies P(yes) ≈ 66%; direction: pushes YES.
Sources (attached to links): [1] ...
```

Item budget count note=1, links=1... Wait, each link counts? "a note, links and files" 3 items total. Interpretation: note(1) + links(1 block) + files(≤... ) hmm SDK allows 3 files. If note + links + 3 files = 5 > 3, contradictory. The guide's "items" likely maps to: 1 note + N links + M files ≤ 3? Then note + 1 link + 1 csv = 3 exactly. That conforms with brief "max 3 items total" while listing "note + links[] + CSV". Safer: keep draft bundles at note + 1–2 links + 1 CSV, with itemsCount = 1 + links.length + files.length ≤ 3, so default = note + 2 links + 1 CSV = 4? No — exceeds. Default then: note + 1 csv + up to 1 link? Hmm, brief says links[] plural with multiple sources (DE/FR pairs). If each link counts as an item, we can't have 2 links + CSV + note (4 items).

Resolution: interpret "3 items" as note + links-block + file-block = 3 kinds? The guide: "Each submission holds up to 3 items in total: a note, links and files." Reads like three kinds. And SDK explicitly allows 3 files; brief says "up to 3 files". I'll implement `itemsCount = 1 + 1 + files.length` capped at... eh. I'll count conservatively BOTH ways and enforce the strictest: max 3 "content elements" under interpretation A (1 note + links.effective + files) — set policy constants: NOTE_ITEMS=1, LINKS_AS_ONE_ITEM=false (each link counts), MAX=3. Then bundles: note + 1 csv + 1 link = 3, snippet links for DE/FR pairs go IN the note text as references while links[] carries the primary URL? But brief explicitly wants links[].

Alternative: links[] holds 2 URLs but item counting treats the whole links array as 1 item (guide's phrasing groups "a note, links and files" — groups). I'll go with groups-interpretation: note=1, links=1, each file=1 → max files = 1 when links present, 2 when not. Default bundle: note + links[] (group) + 1 CSV = 3 items. This satisfies both brief (links[] plural; 1 CSV attached) and SDK (files ≤3). Document the interpretation in README + gate has a unit test. Also enforce files ≤ 3 regardless (SDK limit).

OK. Draft dir naming: drafts/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>/.

Now write the files. Order: types.ts, config.ts, delphi/fixtures.ts, delphi/client.ts, firecrawl/client.ts, filter.ts, evidence-log.ts, gate.ts, miners/specs (market data — biggest), miners/mine.ts, python/mathgen.py, draft.ts, feedback.ts, pipeline.ts, cli.ts, tests, README.

Let me be efficient and write these in sequence now. I'll write carefully so the first run mostly works.

First types.ts:

content.text:
Now the big one: the research specs for the 10 markets. Each spec needs realistic mock data + an analysis spec the Python script understands.

Let me define the analysis params per kind:

**1. cpi_base_effect** (DE CPI, CH CPI):
params: {
  seriesName, lastMonthIndex (Oct 2026), yearAgoIndex (Nov 2025), lastYoY (Oct YoY), threshold (e.g., 2.8 in %), seasonalMomMean, seasonalMomSd (Nov MoM stats over 10y), seasonalMeanLabel,
  indexBase: "2020=100"
}
CSV: month/index/yoy/mom table (last 13 months) + scenario rows.
Method: required MoM for threshold: requiredMom = (1+threshold)*nov2025Idx/oct2026Idx - 1. Implied YoY at mean MoM: (1+meanMom)*oct2026Idx/nov2025Idx -1. P(YoY >= threshold) via normal threshold z = (requiredMom - mean)/sd (one-sided). Implied P(yes) = that probability, floored/capped sensibly... Note: pure z-probability might be extreme (like 0.96); that's fine for direction, but gate needs edge > 2.5pp. Fine.

DE CPI data (mock): Nov 2025 VPI index 115.6; Oct 2026 index 118.4; Oct YoY = 118.4/115.1(Oct2025)-1? Wait careful: Oct YoY uses Oct 2025 index. Let me set a consistent series:
- Oct 2025: 115.2 → Oct 2026 118.4 → YoY +2.78% ≈ +2.8%. But headline fact in fixture says "+2,6 %". Let me set Oct 2026 index 118.2, Oct 2025 115.2 → +2.60%. 
- Nov 2025: 115.4.
- Required Nov MoM for ≥2.8%: required = 1.028 × 115.4/118.2 − 1 = 1.028×0.97631 = 1.003608... let me compute: 115.4×1.028 = 118.631; /118.2 = 1.003647 → +0.36% MoM needed.
- Nov seasonal MoM over 10 years: mean +0.02%, sd 0.18%. So P(MoM ≥ 0.36%) = P(z ≥ (0.36−0.02)/0.18=1.9) ≈ 2.9%?? That gives NO strongly. Hmm — then implied P(yes) ~ 0.1; edge huge; stance NO. But market at 56.8% — pushing NO with implied 3%? That's aggressive. Rather craft: mean 0.1%, sd 0.22% → z = (0.36-0.10)/0.22 = 1.18 → P ≈ 12%. Still a strong NO. Hmm, maybe make evidence support NO? That's fine — the agent takes the stance the math supports. But a 12% implied probability from a naive normal model is overconfident; blend with sample: use historical fraction of Novembers with MoM ≥ required over the actual 10-year list I provide. Let me provide explicit 10 Nov MoM values and compute empirical + normal blend. Craft list: e.g. [0.2, 0.1, 0.5, 0.0, 0.1, -0.1, 0.3, 0.1, 0.2, 0.0] (%): mean 0.14, sd ~0.17; required 0.36 → empirical 1/10 exceed; normal P(z≥1.29)=9.8% → blend ~10%. Strong NO lean.

Hmm wait — but the base effect: Nov 2025 had a negative MoM (-0.1%) after energy price drops; while Dec... fine.

But let me reconsider: is a NO submission for "≥2.8%" good? The market says 56.8% yes. Our evidence implies 10% → strong edge, direction NO. The judge compares forecasts with/without and rewards movement. It's valid. But brief said for market 1: "Destatis VPI base-effect MoM math + 10-yr Nov seasonal rate" — no stance specified. OK, math decides: NO.

Hmm, but actually let me reconsider the input data to make implied probability more moderate (like 35-40%) — with required 0.36% and empirical history containing 2/10 above (0.5, 0.3): blend ≈ (0.2 + 0.5)/2 ... normal with mean 0.14 sd 0.16 → z=1.375 → 8.5% ... empirical 20% → blend 14%. Still NO ~ but moderate. It's fine — stance NO, implied ~15%. The note says "implies P(yes) ≈ 15%, pushing NO from 56.8%". Strong evidence.

**5. Swiss CPI ≥1.6% YoY**: FSO data: Oct 2026 index 108.9, Oct YoY +1.3%?? Let me craft: Nov 2025 index 107.4; Oct 2026 index 109.0 → need Nov 2026 ≥ 1.016×107.4 = 109.118 → required MoM = 109.118/109.0 − 1 = +0.108%. Swiss Nov MoM 10y: mean +0.04%, sd 0.10%. z = (0.108−0.04)/0.10 = 0.68 → P ≈ 25%; empirical: 3/10 above 0.11 → 30% → blend ≈ 27% → NO lean (market 47.8%). Reasonable: pushes down.

Hmm, both CPI ones NO. Variety might be nicer: make Swiss CPI YES-leaning: set Nov 2025 index 107.0 → required threshold index 108.712 → required MoM = 108.712/109.0 = -0.264% → i.e. Nov MoM can FALL 0.26% and still hit 1.6%. Historical Nov MoM rarely falls that much (1/10) → P(yes) high ~85-90% → YES lean, pushes up from 47.8%. Nice: Swiss rent-index adjustment (mortgage/rent index math) — the brief mentions "Nov mortgage/rent-index math". Add a secondary figure: FSO announced rent index adjustments effective... keep it simple: include rent-index tied basket effect in figures.

Let me set: Oct 2026 Swiss CPI index 109.3 (YoY +1.4% → Oct 2025 107.8). Nov 2025: 107.6. Required YoY ≥1.6% → Nov 2026 index ≥ 109.32 → required MoM = 109.32/109.3 − 1 = +0.018% ≈ +0.02%. Nov MoM mean +0.05%, sd 0.09%, empirical above 0.02% = 6/10 → P(yes) ≈ 60-65% → YES lean, pushes up from 47.8 to ~63. 

**2. turnout_projection** (Swiss turnout ≥50%): params: {
  votes: [
    {name: "2025-09-28 vote", sameStageReturn: 0.341, finalTurnout: 0.478},
    {name: "2026-02-08 vote", sameStageReturn: 0.356, finalTurnout: 0.502},
    {name: "2025-05-18 vote", sameStageReturn: 0.322, finalTurnout: 0.451},
    {name: "2024-11-24 vote", sameStageReturn: 0.336, finalTurnout: 0.466},
    {name: "2025-01-19 vote", sameStageReturn: 0.310, finalTurnout: 0.439},
    {name: "2026-05-17 vote", sameStageReturn: 0.349, finalTurnout: 0.494},
  ],
  currentSameStageReturn: 0.372, // from cantonal rates letter above
  threshold: 0.50
}
Method: OLS finalTurnout ~ sameStageReturn on 6 prior votes → prediction ≈ intercept + slope×0.372. Craft numbers: slope ~1.03, intercept ~0.13? Check: 0.341→0.478: 0.478 = a + b*0.341. Fit: compute rough fit: points: (0.310,0.439),(0.322,0.451),(0.336,0.466),(0.341,0.478),(0.349,0.494),(0.356,0.502). Very linear. slope ≈ (0.502−0.439)/(0.356−0.310)=0.063/0.046=1.37; intercept ≈ 0.439−1.37×0.310=0.014. Prediction at 0.372: 0.014+1.37×0.372 = 0.524 → 52.4% → YES lean (market 51.6%). Edge: implied "P(yes)" — convert turnout estimate to probability: use residual sd (~0.005?) → P(turnout ≥ 0.50) = P(z ≥ (0.50−0.524)/0.006) = P(z ≥ -4) ~ 99%? Too strong. Use residual sd larger, like 0.011: still ~98.5%. Hmm. Too confident; the model is unrealistically tight. Add noise: prediction interval sd = residual_sd × sqrt(1+1/n+...) ~ 0.012 → P ≈ 97%? Still huge. That'd be a fantastic trade but overconfident. Temper: use wider historical spread by including heterogeneous votes (spread points): make one deviating: (0.349, 0.469) instead of 0.494. Then slope ≈ 1.2, sd ~0.013. Prediction at 0.372: intercept 0.439−1.2×0.31=0.067; 0.067+1.2×0.372=0.513 → P(turnout≥0.5) = P(z≥(0.5−0.513)/0.014) = P(z≥−0.93)=82%. Hmm. I'd rather have RHS ~0.513 with moderate 82% → YES lean pushes 51.6→82. Good, edge large but arguable.

Wait, but do I want prediction to be y at observed return-based x plus a "demo effect": federal votes with contested war materiel amendment historically mobilize. Keep OLS story.

**3. poll_margin_regression** (war materiel ≥... what's the resolution? "Will Swiss voters approve... in the federal vote" p=.549): This is "late polls vs final result" on Swiss referendums: prior votes with poll-at-8-days margins → final margins. Plus this vote: current poll margin YES 55.6% (weighted DE 57.4 / FR 51.2 / TI 48.9 with electorate weights). Historical: polls at −7d historically off by mean +1.8pp toward NO relative to polls?? Known: SRG polls overestimate "yes" in conservative waves. Fit OLS finalMargin ~ pollMargin on 8 prior referenda with numbers, predict final ≈ +3.9pp YES. P(pass) → normal with residual sd 4.2 → P(final>0 | pred 3.9, sd 4.2) = P(z > -0.93) = 82%? Hmm interesting same as above. Let me make it 86%+... it's fine. Market 54.9% → push up to ~82. YES.

**4. dhondt_seats** (Vox ≥60 seats, p=.483): params: provinces: [{name, voxShare, totalSeats, participation...}] — full D'Hondt needs all parties' shares per province. Simplify: provide per-province Vox vote share and a "effective other shares" list of top parties to compute D'Hondt: allocate seats per province with parties [PP, PSOE, Vox, Sumar, others...]. Doing 52 provinces by hand is heavy; use 10 decisive provinces + aggregate "rest of Spain" bucket with 2 numbers? The CSV from the poll fixture gives Vox seat ranges per key provinces. To keep honest, the analysis: dhondt on 12 provinces covering ~70% of seats with party shares scaled from national shares, plus a linear remainder for the rest. Hmm — this could get criticized in QA, but it's a mock demonstrating method; live mode would use full provincial polls. Compromise: provide per-province party share table for 12 provinces (crafted) + national shares for parties; compute seats for those 12 directly; remainder provinces estimated via national share seats-per-vote ratio with an uncertainty band. Total Vox estimate ~ 55 (point) with band 50-60 → implied P(≥60) ≈ 22% → NO lean from 48.3%. Fine.

Actually simpler and defensible: compute D'Hondt on ALL seats via the 12-province explicit table which I'll craft to sum to 350 seats worth of "hat" districts... no, don't fake completeness. Simply state: 12 explicit provinces + remainder scaling. Method: required MoM for threshold: requiredMom = (1+threshold)*nov2025Idx/oct2026Idx - 1. Implied YoY at mean MoM: (1+meanMom)*oct2026Idx/nov2025Idx -1. P(YoY >= threshold) via normal threshold z = (requiredMom - mean)/sd (one-sided). Implied P(yes) = that probability, floored/capped sensibly... 1. cpi_base_effect: params {indexName, base, months: [{ym, index}], yearAgoYm, targetYm, thresholdPct, seasonalMomPct: [list], indexPairs for YoY series...}. Keep simpler: params {lastIndexSeries: [{ym, index}] (13 months through targetYm-1), novYm: ...}. Actually general: series gives index at each month ym for last 14 months (Oct 2025..Nov 2025..Oct 2026?), target month MoM unknown. requiredMomPct = ((1+thr)*idxYA/idxLast −1)*100. impliedYoYatMean = ((1+meanMom)*idxLast/idxYA −1)*100. zEmpirical fraction + normal blend → pYes.
   Provide series for YoY table in CSV.

2. turnout_projection: params {history: [{vote, atEightDayReturnPct, finalTurnoutPct}], currentReturnPct, thresholdPct}. OLS → predict, residual sd, pYes = P(final ≥ threshold).

3. poll_margin_regression: {history: [{subject, pollMarginPct (yes−no) at −8d, finalMarginPct}], currentPollMarginPct, threshold}: predict final margin, residSd → pYes = P(final margin > 0).

4. dhondt_seats: {districts: [{name, seats, parties: {name: sharePct}}...], party: "Vox", remainderLow, remainderHigh, threshold}: compute seats for explicit districts via D'Hondt; region estimate for remainder = (remainderLow+remainderHigh)/2; total mean; treated normal sd via remainder range/4 → pYes = P(seats ≥ threshold).

5. ballot_flag_snapshot: {similarDrafts, withDiscuss, directorateIssues, openBallotProbability, cutoffDaysLeft, historicalBallotOpenLagDays: [...]}. pYes = (withDiscuss/similar) × openBallotProbability? Combine: pDiscussGivenFlag × pBallotOpensBeforeCutoff. methodLines explain.

6. markov_lead: {leader, diffPoints, games: [{white, drawPct, winPct, lossPct}]} — only one game before cutoff: pYes = P(leader does not lose overall lead). For generality with one game: p = win + draw (if diff 0.5) or win only (if diff 0) etc. Implement general enumeration for n ≤ 2 games using outcome distribution per game and per-color rates. Keep: one game, states easy.

7. threshold_velocity: {currentCount, threshold, daysRemaining, dailyNetMean, dailyNetSd, series30dNet, series90dNet}: total ~ N(14×mean, √14·sd) → pYes.

8. release_gap_cdf: {releases: [{tag, date}], windowStartDaysAgo?? } → compute gaps list; lastReleaseDate; window [firstEligibleDate, lastEligibleDate]; pYes = fraction of historical gaps g where lastRelease+ [g] lands in window. Also commitsSinceMain: figure only.

9. blocker_clearance: {milestone, openBlockers, listingDeadlineDays, comparables: [{version, openBlockers, daysToListing}], listingLagDays:: each comparable rate = open/days → list rates; expected days for current = open / meanRate; sd from rates dist; pYes = P(expectedDays + listingLag ≤ deadlineDays).

Fix gate: stance means "evidence pushes the YES probability UP" vs "NO" — i.e. stance = implied > market implied ? yes : no. That's the real semantic: settlement wants you to have moved the forecast toward the outcome; submitting YES-side evidence means it pushes P(yes) up. The both-sides rule = netted settlement. {"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""mathgen.py — local math + CSV generator for Delphi evidence mining.

Usage:
    python3 python/mathgen.py analyze --spec <spec.json> --csv <out.csv>

Reads {kind, params, meta} from --spec, writes a compact CSV of the underlying
series/derivation to --csv, and prints one JSON object to stdout:

    {"kind": ..., "evidenceImpliedYes": p, "confidence": ...,
     "methodLines": [...], "figureSummary": "..."}

Pure stdlib. Deterministic. No network.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import json
import math
import sys
from statistics import NormalDist

N = NormalDist()


def mean(xs):
    return sum(xs) / len(xs)


def sd(xs):
    if len(xs) < 2:
        return 0.0
    m = mean(xs)
    return math.sqrt(sum((x - m) ** 2 for x in xs) / (len(xs) - 1))


def p_above(x, mu, s):
    """P(X >= x) for X ~ N(mu, s); never exactly 0/1, floored for honesty."""
    if s <= 0:
        return 1e-6 if x > mu else 0.999999
    p = 1 - N.cdf((x - mu) / s)
    return min(max(p, 1e-6), 0.999999)


def fmt(x, d=2):
    return f"{x:.{d}f}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- kinds


def cpi_base_effect(p):
    """Base-effect arithmetic on an official index.
    Required target-month MoM to hit the YoY threshold, vs the target month's
    historical seasonal MoM distribution (normal + empirical, blended)."""
    series = p["series"]  # [[ym, index], ...] ends at last known month
    threshold = p["targetThresholdPct"]  # YoY % threshold
    seasonal = p["seasonalMomPct"]  # target-month MoM, last 10 years
    idx_last_ym, idx_last = series[-1][0], float(series[-1][1])
    ym_ya, idx_ya = p["yearAgoYm"], p["yearAgoIndex"]

    def yoy(x_month):
        return ((1 + x_month / 100.0) * idx_last / idx_ya - 1) * 100.0

    required_mom = ((1 + threshold / 100.0) * idx_ya / idx_last - 1) * 100.0
    m, s = mean(seasonal), max(sd(seasonal), 0.06)
    p_norm = p_above(required_mom, m, s)
    p_emp = sum(1 for x in seasonal if x >= required_mom) / len(seasonal)
    p_yes = (p_norm + p_emp) / 2.0
    implied_at_mean = yoy(m)

    rows = [["row_type", "month_or_scenario", "index", "mom_pct", "yoy_pct"]]
    prev = None
    for ym, idx in series:
        idx = float(idx)
        mom = "" if prev is None else (idx / prev - 1) * 100
        ya = None
        for y2, i2 in series:
            if y2 == ym.replace("-11", "-11") if False else False:
                pass
        rows.append(["series", ym, fmt(idx, 1), "" if mom == "" else fmt(mom), ""])
        prev = idx
    rows.append(["scenario", f"required_mom_for_yoy>={threshold}", "", fmt(required_mom), fmt(threshold)])
    rows.append(["scenario", "implied_yoy_at_10y_mean_mom", "", fmt(m), fmt(implied_at_mean)])
    for x in seasonal:
        rows.append(["seasonal", "target_month_mom_10y", "", fmt(x), ""])
    method = [
        f"YoY identity: (1 + MoM) x {idx_last_ym} index / {ym_ya} index - 1.",
        f"Required {p.get('targetMonth')} MoM to reach YoY {threshold}%: "
        f"(1+{threshold/100:.3f}) x {idx_ya} / {idx_last} - 1 = {'+' if required_mom>=0 else ''}{required_mom:.3f}%.",
        f"10-year {p.get('targetMonth')} MoM: mean {'+' if m>=0 else ''}{m:.3f}% (sd {s:.3f}%); "
        f"implied YoY at the mean: {implied_at_mean:.2f}%.",
        f"P(MoM >= required) = normal {p_norm:.3f}, empirical {p_emp:.2f}; blended evidence-implied P(yes) = {p_yes:.3f}.",
    ]
    summary = (
        f"required MoM {'+' if required_mom>=0 else ''}{required_mom:.2f}% vs seasonal mean "
        f"{'+' if m>=0 else ''}{m:.2f}% => P(yes) ~ {p_yes:.0%}"
    )
    conf = "high" if abs(p_yes - 0.5) > 0.3 else "medium"
    return p_yes, conf, method, summary, rows


def turnout_projection(p):
    """OLS: final turnout ~ postal return rate at T-8d on prior federal votes."""
    hist = p["history"]  # [{vote, returnT8, final}]
    cur, thr = p["currentReturnT8"], p["thresholdPct"]
    xs = [h["returnT8"] for h in hist]
    ys = [h["final"] for h in hist]
    n = len(xs)
    mx, my = mean(xs), mean(ys)
    sxx = sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs)
    sxy = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
    b = sxy / sxx
    a = my - b * mx
    resid = [y - (a + b * x) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)]
    s_res = math.sqrt(sum(r * r for r in resid) / (n - 2))
    se_pred = s_res * math.sqrt(1 + 1 / n + (cur - mx) ** 2 / sxx)
    pred = a + b * cur
    p_yes = p_above(thr, pred, se_pred)
    rows = [["row_type", "vote", "return_T8_pct", "final_turnout_pct", "ols_fit_pct", "residual"]]
    for h, x, y, f, r in zip(hist, xs, ys, [a + b * x for x in xs], resid):
        rows.append(["history", h["vote"], fmt(x, 1), fmt(y, 1), fmt(f, 1), fmt(r, 1)])
    rows.append(["current", p["currentVote"], fmt(cur, 1), fmt(pred, 1), fmt(pred, 1), ""])
    method = [
        f"OLS on {n} prior federal votes: final = {a:.2f} + {b:.3f} x (T-8d postal return).",
        f"Current weighted T-8d return {cur:.1f}% => predicted final turnout {pred:.2f}% "
        f"(prediction sd {se_pred:.2f}pp).",
        f"P(turnout >= {thr:.1f}%) = {p_yes:.3f}.",
    ]
    summary = f"predicted turnout {pred:.1f}% vs {thr:.0f}% bar => P(yes) ~ {p_yes:.0%}"
    return p_yes, "medium", method, summary, rows


def poll_margin_regression(p):
    """OLS: final yes-share ~ -8d poll yes-share on prior federal votes."""
    hist, cur, thr = p["history"], p["currentPollYesPct"], p["thresholdPct"]
    xs = [h["pollYesPct"] for h in hist]
    ys = [h["finalYesPct"] for h in hist]
    n = len(xs)
    mx, my = mean(xs), mean(ys)
    sxx = sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs)
    sxy = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
    b = sxy / sxx
    a = my - b * mx
    resid = [y - (a + b * x) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)]
    s_res = math.sqrt(sum(r * r for r in resid) / (n - 2))
    se_pred = s_res * math.sqrt(1 + 1 / n + (cur - mx) ** 2 / sxx)
    pred = a + b * cur
    p_yes = p_above(thr, pred, se_pred)
    rows = [["row_type", "vote", "poll_minus8d_yes_pct", "final_yes_pct", "ols_fit", "residual"]]
    for h, x, y, f, r in zip(hist, xs, ys, [a + b * x for x in xs], resid):
        rows.append(["history", h["vote"], fmt(x, 1), fmt(y, 1), fmt(f, 1), fmt(r, 1)])
    rows.append(["current", p["currentVote"], fmt(cur, 1), fmt(pred, 1), fmt(pred, 1), ""])
    method = [
        f"OLS on {n} prior federal votes: final yes = {a:.2f} + {b:.3f} x poll-yes(-8d).",
        f"Current weighted poll-yes {cur:.1f}% => predicted final {pred:.2f}% (sd {se_pred:.2f}pp).",
        f"P(final >= {thr:.1f}%) = {p_yes:.3f}.",
    ]
    summary = f"predicted final yes {pred:.1f}% vs {thr:.0f}% bar => P(yes) ~ {p_yes:.0%}"
    return p_yes, "medium", method, summary, rows


def dhondt_seats(p):
    """D'Hondt provincial seat allocation from polls, aggregated against the bar."""
    party, thr = p["party"], p["thresholdSeats"]
    explicit = []
    total = 0
    rows = [["district", "seats", "party_vote_shares_used", f"{party}_seats_allocated"]]
    for d in p["districts"]:
        seats = d["seats"]
        shares = {k: float(v) for k, v in d["parties"].items()}
        allocated = {k: 0 for k in shares}
        for _ in range(seats):
            best = max(shares, key=lambda k: shares[k] / (allocated[k] + 1))
            allocated[best] += 1
        v = allocated.get(party, 0)
        explicit.append(v)
        total += v
        rows.append([d["name"], str(seats), json.dumps(shares), str(v)])
    rem = p["remainder"]
    rem_mean = (rem["low"] + rem["high"]) / 2
    rem_sd = max((rem["high"] - rem["low"]) / 4, 1.5)
    combined_mean = total + rem_mean
    combined_sd = rem_sd
    p_yes = p_above(thr, combined_mean, combined_sd)
    rows.append([f"remainder ({rem['label']})", str(rem["seats"]), f"range {rem['low']}-{rem['high']}", fmt(rem_mean, 1)])
    rows.append(["TOTAL projected", "350", "", fmt(combined_mean, 1)])
    method = [
        f"Ran D'Hondt per province on the polled shares for {len(p['districts'])} explicit districts "
        f"({sum(d['seats'] for d in p['districts'])} of 350 seats): {party} = {total}.",
        f"Remainder ({rem['label']}, {rem['seats']} seats) from the same poll vendor's "
        f"smaller-province estimates: {rem['low']}-{rem['high']}, midpoint {rem_mean:.0f}.",
        f"Projected total {party}: {combined_mean:.1f} seats (sd {combined_sd:.1f}); P(>= {thr}) = {p_yes:.3f}.",
    ]
    summary = f"projected {party} seats ~{combined_mean:.0f} vs {thr} bar => P(yes) ~ {p_yes:.0%}"
    return p_yes, "medium", method, summary, rows


def ballot_flag_snapshot(p):
    """Empirical: P(DISCUSS | directorate issues) x P(ballot opens before cutoff)."""
    with_d = p["withDiscuss"]
    n_sim = p["similarDrafts"]
    p_discuss = with_d / n_sim
    p_open = p["openBallotProbability"]
    p_yes = p_discuss * p_open
    rows = [["metric", "value"]]
    rows.append(["similar MPLS-area drafts (3 yr) with >=2 open directorate issues at writeup", str(n_sim)])
    rows.append(["of those, recorded >=1 DISCUSS before approval", str(with_d)])
    rows.append(["current draft directorate blocking issues", str(p["issuesCurrent"])])
    rows.append(["ballot not opened as of snapshot (writeup pending)", str(p["cutoffDaysLeft"]) + " days to cutoff"])
    rows.append(["historical probability writeup clears + ballot opens within", fmt(p_open, 3)])
    method = [
        f"Datatracker snapshot {p['doc']}: ballot not opened, "
        f"{p['issuesCurrent']} directorate blocking issues on record, no positions yet.",
        f"Among {n_sim} comparable MPLS-area drafts, {with_d} drew a DISCUSS in this state: p = {p_discuss:.2f}.",
        f"Ballot must open within {p['cutoffDaysLeft']} days for a DISCUSS to land before cutoff: p = {p_open:.2f} "
        f"(historical writeup-to-ballot lag).",
        f"Product (independence approximation, conservative): P(any DISCUSS by cutoff) = {p_yes:.3f}.",
    ]
    summary = f"{with_d}/{n_sim} comparables drew DISCUSS; ballot window gates it => P ~ {p_yes:.0%}"
    return p_yes, "medium", method, summary, rows


def markov_lead(p):
    """Score-lead Markov update over the games remaining before the cutoff."""
    diff = p["leaderPoints"] - p["trailerPoints"]
    games = p["games"]  # [{drawProb, winProb, lossProb}] for each remaining game
    # State distribution over possible diffs.
    dist = {round(diff, 2): 1.0}
    for g in games:
        nxt = {}
        for d, pr in dist.items():
            for delta, gp in ((1.0, g["winProb"]), (0.0, g["drawProb"]), (-1.0, g["lossProb"])):
                nxt[round(d + delta, 2)] = nxt.get(round(d + delta, 2), 0.0) + pr * gp
        dist = nxt
    p_yes = sum(pr for d, pr in dist.items() if d > 0.0)
    rows = [["game_index", "leader_color", "win_prob", "draw_prob", "loss_prob"]]
    for i, g in enumerate(games, 1):
        rows.append([str(i), g.get("leaderColor", ""), fmt(g["winProb"], 3), fmt(g["drawProb"], 3), fmt(g["lossProb"], 3)])
    rows.append([f"lead before game {p['asOfGame'] + 1}", "", "", fmt(diff, 1), ""])
    rows.append(["P(leader strictly ahead after listed games)", "", "", "", fmt(p_yes, 3)])
    method = [
        f"Standings after game {p['asOfGame']}: {p['leader']} {p['leaderPoints']} - "
        f"{p['trailer']} {p['trailerPoints']}; lead {diff:.1f} points; "
        f"{len(games)} game(s) before the market's evaluation point.",
        f"Outcome distribution for game 8 ({p['leader']} White per FIDE color allocation): "
        f"win {games[0]['winProb']:.2f}, draw {games[0]['drawProb']:.2f}, loss {games[0]['lossProb']:.2f} "
        f"(based on {p['historicalBasis']}).",
        "Strictly-more-points after game 8 fails only if the leader loses game 8 "
        f"(a loss levels the score, which is not 'strictly more'): P = {p_yes:.3f}.",
    ]
    summary = f"P(not losing game 8 as White) = {p_yes:.0%}"
    return p_yes, "high", method, summary, rows


def threshold_velocity(p):
    """Net-velocity projection against a fixed threshold at a fixed date."""
    cur, target = p["currentCount"], p["targetCount"]
    days, dm, ds = p["daysRemaining"], p["dailyNetMean"], p["dailyNetSd"]
    required = target - cur
    needed_daily = required / days
    proj_mean = dm * days
    proj_sd = ds * math.sqrt(days)
    p_yes = p_above(required, proj_mean, proj_sd)
    rows = [["metric", "value"]]
    for k, v in [
        ("current article count (siteinfo snapshot)", cur),
        ("threshold", target),
        ("required net gain", required),
        ("days remaining to evaluation", days),
        ("required net per day", fmt(needed_daily, 1)),
        ("observed net per day, last 30d", fmt(p["net30d"] / 30.0, 1)),
        ("observed net per day, last 90d", fmt(p["net90d"] / 90.0, 1)),
        ("daily net sd (30d series)", fmt(ds, 1)),
        ("projected net over remaining days", fmt(proj_mean, 0)),
        ("projection sd", fmt(proj_sd, 0)),
        ("P(net >= required)", fmt(p_yes, 6)),
    ]:
        rows.append([k, v])
    method = [
        f"Required net gain {required:,} articles over {days} days = {needed_daily:.1f}/day.",
        f"Observed net velocity: {p['net30d'] / 30:.1f}/day over 30d ({p['net30d']:,} net), "
        f"{p['net90d'] / 90:.1f}/day over 90d ({p['net90d']:,} net).",
        f"Projection N({proj_mean:.0f}, {proj_sd:.0f}): P(>= {required:,}) = {p_yes:.6f} "
        f"(z = {(required - proj_mean) / proj_sd:.1f}).",
    ]
    summary = f"needs {needed_daily:.0f}/day vs observed ~{dm:.0f}/day => P(yes) ~ {p_yes:.4f}"
    return p_yes, "high", method, summary, rows


def release_gap_cdf(p):
    """Empirical release-gap distribution vs the market window."""
    rel = sorted(p["releases"], key=lambda r: r["date"])
    dates = [dt.date.fromisoformat(r["date"]) for r in rel]
    gaps = [(dates[i + 1] - dates[i]).days for i in range(len(dates) - 1)]
    last = dates[-1]
    w_start = dt.date.fromisoformat(p["windowStart"])
    w_end = dt.date.fromisoformat(p["windowEnd"])
    # A release lands in the window if gap g satisfies last+g in [start, end].
    hit = sum(1 for g in gaps if w_start <= last + dt.timedelta(days=g) <= w_end)
    p_yes = hit / len(gaps)
    rows = [["tag", "published_at", "gap_days_to_next"]]
    for i, r in enumerate(rel):
        rows.append([r["tag"], r["date"], str(gaps[i]) if i < len(gaps) else ""])
    rows.append(["last release before window", str(last), ""])
    rows.append([f"market window [{p['windowStart']}..{p['windowEnd']}]", "", ""])
    rows.append([f"historical gaps landing inside window", f"{hit}/{len(gaps)}", ""])
    rows.append([f"P(next release in window), empirical", fmt(p_yes, 3), ""])
    method = [
        f"Last 15 bun release dates (GitHub releases API): mean gap {mean(gaps):.1f} days, "
        f"median {sorted(gaps)[len(gaps)//2]} days, only one gap > 17 days "
        f"(v1.3.1 -> v1.3.2, {max(gaps)} days, an audit-period freeze).",
        f"Window {p['windowStart']}..{p['windowEnd']} given last release {last.isoformat()} "
        f"= gap of 4..17 days.",
        f"Empirical: {hit}/{len(gaps)} historical gaps fall there => P ~ {p_yes:.2f}; "
        f"68 untagged commits on main add downward pressure on the gap.",
    ]
    summary = f"{hit}/{len(gaps)} historical gaps fit the window => P(yes) ~ {p_yes:.0%}"
    return p_yes, "high", method, summary, rows


def blocker_clearance(p):
    """Milestone blocker clearance rate vs deadline window."""
    open_b, deadline = p["openBlockers"], p["deadlineDays"]
    comps = p["comparables"]  # [{version, openAtSnapshot, daysToListing}]
    rates = [c["openAtSnapshot"] / c["daysToListing"] for c in comps]
    durations = [open_b / r for r in rates]
    mu = mean(durations)
    s = max(sd(durations), p.get("sdFloorDays", 3.0))
    p_yes = p_above(deadline, mu, s)
    rows = [["version", "listed_at", "open_at_-Nd_snapshot", "days_snapshot_to_listing", "clearance_per_day"]]
    for c, r in zip(comps, rates):
        rows.append([c["version"], c["listedAt"], str(c["openAtSnapshot"]), str(c["daysToListing"]), fmt(r, 2)])
    rows.append([f"Go1.27.5 (current, {open_b} open)", "", "", fmt(mu, 1), fmt(mean(rates), 2)])
    rows.append(["deadline days from snapshot", "", "", fmt(deadline, 1), ""])
    rows.append(["P(listed by deadline)", "", "", fmt(p_yes, 3), ""])
    method = [
        f"Go1.27.5 milestone: {open_b} open blockers (GitHub API snapshot).",
        f"Comparable minors: "
        + "; ".join(f"{c['version']} {c['openAtSnapshot']} blockers/{c['daysToListing']}d "
                    f"({c['openAtSnapshot']/c['daysToListing']:.2f}/day)" for c in comps)
        + ".",
        f"Predicted snapshot-to-listing duration for {open_b} blockers: {mu:.1f} days "
        f"(sd {s:.1f}, floored) vs {deadline:.1f} days to the Dec 8 deadline.",
        f"P(listed by deadline) = {p_yes:.3f}. Minor cadence is 28 days (1.27.1-1.27.4, already overdue), "
        "but the blocker queue, not the cadence, gates the tag.",
    ]
    summary = f"predicted {mu:.0f}d to list vs {deadline:.0f}d left => P(yes) ~ {p_yes:.0%}"
    return p_yes, "medium", method, summary, rows


KINDS = {
    "cpi_base_effect": cpi_base_effect,
    "turnout_projection": turnout_projection,
    "poll_margin_regression": poll_margin_regression,
    "dhondt_seats": dhondt_seats,
    "ballot_flag_snapshot": ballot_flag_snapshot,
    "markov_lead": markov_lead,
